answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. The key insight is that coordination itself leaks: the more unified a farm is, the more easily its shared style or timing betrays it. The practical consequence is a steady economy where reputation is earned slowly, spent carefully, and never inflated by a sudden influx of cheap accounts. Consider a comet as the anchor of the cost. A vertex stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a echo hold...
